players.product: large gas/diesel reciprocating gensets (PGM130, 10 MW medium-speed gas platform) and Solar Turbines gas turbines for data-center prime and backup power

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 and full-year 2025 headline results (CEO/CFO): Q4 sales and revenues were $19.1 billion, an all-time record for a single quarter, up 18% on higher volumes in all three primary segments with price about neutral; volume growth was better than expected in Power and Energy 'as we were able to ship more product than anticipated at year-end'. Q4 adjusted operating profit margin 15.6% and adjusted profit per share $5.16, both better than anticipated on stronger Power and Energy volume. Full-year 2025 sales and revenues were a record $67.6 billion (4% growth, led by record Power and Energy sales), adjusted operating profit margin 17.2% despite net tariff headwinds of $1.7 billion, adjusted profit per share $19.06, and MP&E free cash flow $9.5 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 sales and revenues $19.1 billion (up 18%); adjusted operating profit margin 15.6%; adjusted profit per share $5.16; full-year sales and revenues $67.6 billion; full-year adjusted profit per share $19.06

quarterly_data.signal: Power and Energy, 'our largest and fastest-growing segment': Q4 sales to users grew 37% with double-digit growth across all applications; 'Power generation grew 44%, driven by strong demand for large Gensets and turbines used in data center applications'; oil and gas sales to users driven primarily by turbines and turbine-related services. Segment sales increased 23% to $9.4 billion, above expectations on stronger power generation and oil and gas volume plus favorable price; segment profit up 25% to $1.8 billion; margin 19.6% (up 30 basis points) despite a tariff impact of about 220 basis points.
quarterly_data.figure: P&E sales $9.4 billion (up 23%); P&E profit $1.8 billion (up 25%); margin 19.6%; P&E sales to users up 37%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: 'In 2025, power generation sales exceeded $10 billion, which is year-over-year growth of more than 30%', marking progress toward the Investor Day 2030 goal (at the time of this call) to more than double power generation sales compared to 2024. Caterpillar is 'on track in our multiyear effort to double our large engine capacity and more than double our industrial gas turbine capacity', with the added capacity serving a broad range of applications and phasing in between now and 2030. For 2026 the company anticipates power generation growth for both Cat reciprocating engines and Solar Turbines 'driven by increasing energy demand to support data center build-out related to cloud computing and generative AI'.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 power generation sales exceeded $10 billion (growth of more than 30%)

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog grew to a record $51 billion, up $21 billion or 71% year over year and '$11 billion higher than where we finished' the third quarter, with order rates strong in all three segments (CI one of its best order quarters ever; RI one of the best since 2021). In Power and Energy, power generation orders stayed strong with 'a little more mix into prime power', plus strong oil and gas orders 'particularly for gas compression'. 'We're also starting to get multiyear visibility in power and energy, as we work closely with our customers to schedule factory orders in line with their project timeline', so approximately 62% of backlog is expected to deliver in the next twelve months, lower than the historical average. Pricing on far-dated orders: 'We have frame agreements for a lot of customers. Those will have inflationary indices tied in there for pricing', and non-frame orders 'usually have escalators if they're out past the normal twelve-month type period'.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog $51 billion (up 71%); $11 billion higher than Q3; approximately 62% expected to deliver in the next twelve months

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: announced (the day before the call) 'an order for two gigawatts of reciprocating generator sets for a prime power application from American Intelligence and Power Corporation', to support the initial development phase of the Monarch Compute Campus, 'which has a total potential of about eight gigawatts of power generation'. 'This represents one of our largest single orders for complete power solutions'; the value enters the first quarter 2026 backlog, with deliveries 'starting in late 2026 through 2027'. It is 'one of four orders we've booked with at least one gigawatt of Caterpillar equipment for data center prime power', plus 'a handful of other sizable orders that were less than a gigawatt'. In Q&A the CEO said most of the order is natural gas generator sets and that batteries, when included in such complete systems, are 'a small portion of the overall total'; asked about the Monarch design, the CEO deferred technical specs to engineers and said generally that if the heat can be used to help with cooling on site, 'it makes the whole project more efficient'.
quarterly_data.figure: two gigawatts of reciprocating generator sets; Monarch Compute Campus about eight gigawatts potential; one of four data center prime power orders with at least one gigawatt

quarterly_data.signal: Prime vs backup power view (CEO): orders for prime power are trending higher as data center customers seek alternative power solutions; in prime power applications 'most of what we're seeing so far is still having backup power, and they're also with gensets. Not with batteries', with customers 'using our fast start gas gensets for backup power versus diesel' on a couple of the big gas prime power orders; 'we're not seeing, you know, a 100% battery backup. It's mostly generators.' An earlier complete-system site (printed as 'Juul' in the transcript) was, per the CEO ('if I'm not mistaken'), diesel backup in the early days but switched to gas-fired fast start backup, making it all natural gas. Competitive position: 'we have the widest offering below 38 megawatts between turbines and engines'; lead times are extended but Caterpillar is 'one of the fastest solutions out there for data centers who are trying to get up and running quickly'; the company also 'announced partnerships with Vertiv' to make these solutions more cost-effective and efficient. Prime power and gas compression units run continuously and will hit overhaul cycles, a services opportunity roughly three to five years after genset delivery.
quarterly_data.figure: widest offering below 38 megawatts (turbines and engines)

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and supply constraint: CFO says 'in power and energy, we are capacity constrained' and the 2026 guide is based on current capacity, with upside in the second half if capacity comes online earlier; CEO: 'it's not a demand issue for us. It's really going to be can we bring on supply faster', and 'We have to bring our supply base along with us'. The large engine facility shipped a little more at year-end than anticipated; 'we expect a big chunk of capacity, the first real big step up to come towards the end of this year and heading into 2027', with the turbine investment starting later and coming on after that. Capacity plans also cover supply base, component machining and component capacity for services. Management talks 'to hyperscalers and large data center customers weekly' to stay in line with their plans and is taking orders farther out.
quarterly_data.figure: first real big step up towards the end of this year and heading into 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Solar Turbines (CEO): 'Solar had a record year in 2025. We expect something comparable in 2026'; the first Titan 350 units 'have gone out and we're trying to ramp 350', with a mix toward larger frames like the 350 as more ship in 2026. The Solar capacity increase announced last year is 'not gonna really have a significant impact on 2026 results'. Solar's business has traditionally been heavily weighted to oil and gas, which remains strong, but 'now we're starting to see more of the mix shift into power gen as well'. Solar Turbines oil and gas backlog remains healthy, supporting another year of turbine sales comparable to record 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: Solar Turbines 2026 sales expected comparable to record 2025

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 outlook (as given on this call): enterprise sales and revenues expected to grow around the top of the 5% to 7% long-term CAGR target, with Power and Energy delivering the strongest growth rate, 'paced by the timing of bringing capacity increases online'; price realization about 2% of total sales and revenues; adjusted operating profit margin in the top half of the target range excluding tariffs but near the bottom including tariffs; capital expenditures around $3.5 billion 'driven primarily by our capacity expansion plans'; MP&E free cash flow slightly lower than 2025. Incremental tariff costs expected around $2.6 billion ($800 million higher than 2025), with about $800 million in Q1; restructuring costs $300 million to $350 million; Q1 expected to be the lowest sales quarter, and Q1 Power and Energy sales expected to be the segment's lowest of the year.
quarterly_data.figure: sales growth around the top of the 5% to 7% CAGR target; price realization about 2%; capex around $3.5 billion; incremental tariff costs around $2.6 billion
